tasks.short: Recommend changes to improve crew efficiency

steps.what: Assess working conditions and equipment and recommend changes to increase crew efficiency

tasks.design: Keep contextual assessment and recommendations with the supervisor. Existing records in {OPS_SYSTEM} can inform discussion, but recorded output alone does not explain site conditions or establish a better work method.
tasks.previous_blocker: Efficiency changes involve practical trade-offs and crew knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: Operational records can inform judgement without replacing site understanding.
tasks.still_hard: A faster method may reduce quality or increase physical strain.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor tests whether an apparent improvement is workable and acceptable to the crew.
tasks.altitude: Recommendation time and authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss the physical-work effects of a proposed equipment change
reach.learn: Ergonomic trade-offs and safe work trials

evidence.claim: Retaining contextual crew-efficiency recommendations is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is assessing and recommending, not management approval, equipment procurement or implementation.
No free structured efficiency-cause flag is presumed; observed conditions and crew accounts need interpretation.
Retain native records; no custom recommendation tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes.
unknowns: Recurring work constraints and crew involvement
research_questions: Which apparent efficiency losses are explained by site or safety conditions?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; assessment and recommendation keep full time without assumed report-production work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer customers about methods, materials and price ranges

steps.what: Locate current method, material and indicative price information for customer inquiries
Answer inquiries, clarify site needs and explain limits of indicative price ranges

tasks.design: Configure native keyword search and a current service index in {DOCS}. The supervisor reads the source and answers personally, distinguishing indicative ranges from site-specific quotes; no generated answer or automatic customer commitment is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scattered method and price documents prolong routine lookup.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document search and approved links can shorten navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Site conditions and customer priorities affect suitability and actual price.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor recognises when a generic range is misleading.
tasks.altitude: Reduce lookup effort while keeping the customer conversation and pricing authority unchanged.

reach.task: Handle routine service-information enquiries from approved material

evidence.claim: Native document search for approved service information is an E1 design from model knowledge; the digest supplies no measured customer-inquiry saving.

assumptions: Boundary is lookup and answering, excluding preparing estimates and negotiating fees.

Existing service owners produce approved method sheets and price lists. Supervisor s1 enters search terms and verifies date, version and applicability within its remaining18 hours; no structured suitable-method or binding-price flag is assumed.
Missing or contradictory information returns to manual source checking; native keyword search comes before custom code.
Document-index upkeep is costed below; no new capture work is transferred for free.
unknowns: Current document quality and actual lookup share
research_questions: Does indexed lookup save time after checking price currency and applicability?

incremental.description: Check index links and flag stale service information

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R88 gross12 minus4 upkeep gives net8. E1 scenario: incomplete indexing and longer source checks reduce net to2-7; the70-hour conversation retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Survey sprinkler needs and select candidate pipe, valve and coverage parameters
Calculate pressure losses, flows and coverage for candidate sprinkler layouts
Check hydraulic assumptions and coverage, revise the design and approve the installation plan
Supervise sprinkler installation and resolve actual site deviations

tasks.design: Use checked formulas in {SPREADSHEET} for repeated arithmetic on supervisor-verified inputs. The supervisor validates hydraulic assumptions and the exact plan in {DOCS}, then retains site supervision; formulas do not choose a safe or suitable design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeating calculations across candidate layouts costs time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing spreadsheet formulas can calculate fixed hydraulic and coverage expressions.
tasks.still_hard: Supply measurements, equipment curves and actual site conditions can invalidate assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor judges practical coverage and installation constraints.

ambition.what: Compare an additional feasible sprinkler zone layout before installation

tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic with unchanged design approval and site responsibility.

reach.task: Compare calculations for alternative zone layouts

evidence.claim: Automating repeated sprinkler arithmetic from verified measurements is an E1 design from model knowledge, not a capability established by the cleaning-software digest.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor survey, design calculation and installation oversight; crew installation labour is excluded.

Supervisor s1 measures and captures site dimensions, elevations, supply pressure and flow with units, pipe lengths and diameters, material coefficients, valve losses, emitter curves, spacing and zone assignments. All selection, measurement and capture stays in35 hours; missing or incompatible data returns to manual specialist calculation.
Native checked formulas precede custom code; s3 checks model applicability, units and actual coverage and repeats approval after changes.
Existing installation crew executes the plan between s3 and s4 through unchanged work; any extra trials for the optional ambition are additional work outside savings.
unknowns: Existing formula tools, measurement quality and supervisor design authority
research_questions: Do checked formulas reproduce accepted designs including field measurement, review and revision time?

incremental.description: Formula regression checks and specification updates

approvals.approved_version: Exact layout, inputs, calculation revision, equipment and zone plan; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gross20 minus4 upkeep gives net16. E1 repeat-layout scenario; additional measurement and verification can reduce net to4-12 while survey, review and supervision stay fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Negotiate fees and service trade-offs with customers within approved commercial limits

tasks.design: Retain customer negotiation and explanation of service trade-offs. An existing estimate in {CRM} informs the conversation; preparing that estimate belongs to its own task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreement depends on priorities, trust and acceptable scope changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Calculation tools can inform negotiation without conducting it.
tasks.still_hard: A lower fee can conceal an unacceptable reduction in scope or quality.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor recognises customer priorities and protects practical delivery commitments.
tasks.altitude: Negotiation time and delegated authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain scope and fee trade-offs in a customer discussion
reach.learn: Commercial boundaries and explicit scope agreement

evidence.claim: Retaining fee negotiation is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is negotiation, excluding estimate preparation and contract execution.
The existing estimating task produces the service estimate and management supplies commercial limits; no free structured acceptable-fee flag is assumed.
Retain native estimate access; no custom negotiation tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; assign overlapping customer-information conversations once.
research_questions: Which fee requests require management approval rather than supervisor discretion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; customer negotiation keeps full time, excluding separately owned estimate work.
